title: Hold a kebab skewer up with one hand and push four pieces onto it with the other
instruction: Hold the skewer level by its handle with one hand. With the other, set each kebab piece in the prep stand's channel, hole toward the skewer's point, and push it onto the point and up the skewer until all four pieces are on. Then lay the skewer back across the grill and let go.
context: Threading food onto skewers is routine line-cook and food-prep work: one hand holds the skewer steady while the other pushes the pieces on. A skewer lying on the grill rests on its point, so it has to be lifted and held while the pieces go on.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed dark steel grill tray, 14 cm front to back, centred 25 cm forward, with charcoal in it (looks only, no fire): its left side wall 2.5 cm thick and 3.9 cm tall, 12 to 14.5 cm left of the centre line; its right side wall 4 cm thick and 5 cm tall, 10 to 14 cm right of it; low front and back walls 3 cm tall. (2) A loose kebab skewer lying left to right across the side walls, 25 cm forward: a round steel blade 4 mm across and 24.1 cm long (its last 1.6 cm narrowing to a point), a steel collar 2.8 x 2.8 cm and 3 mm thick, and a flat wooden handle 12 cm long, 1.4 cm wide and 2.6 cm tall; 70 g, balancing 1.8 cm in front of the collar. Its collar is 10 cm left of the centre line, its handle rests on the left wall and its point on the right wall, flush with that wall's outer face. (3) Four loose kebab pieces, 10 g each: blocks 3 cm wide, 2.6 cm long and 3 cm tall with a hole 1.2 cm wide and 1.6 cm tall through their length (two brown meat pieces, a green pepper and a cream onion), standing in a row on a fixed light wooden cutting board (7 x 17 cm, 1.2 cm thick) 38 cm forward, 12, 16, 20 and 24 cm right of the centre line, their holes running left to right. (4) A fixed light grey steel prep stand 25 cm forward, from 14.4 to 19.1 cm right of the centre line: a pillar 4.2 cm wide whose top, 9.1 cm above the table, has a smooth channel 3.4 cm wide between two rails 4 mm high, running left to right in line with the skewer. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. A piece is on the skewer when the blade runs through its hole: its centre within 8 mm of the blade's axis, between the collar and the point. The skewer lies across the grill when its axis is within 10 degrees of level and crosses over both side walls no more than 2.5 cm above their tops, with every piece between the walls. A gripper has let go when its fingertip centre (TCP) is at least 4 cm from the skewer's axis and from every piece. 1.0: all four pieces on the skewer, the skewer across the grill, both grippers let go; 0.5: all four on the skewer; 0.25: at least one on it; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with everything still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: slide the pieces off the skewer, stand them back on the board and lay the skewer back across the grill.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the pieces are solid with the hole's mouths printed on; once the skewer's point is in a hole's mouth, lined up within 15 degrees, a joint keeps the piece on the blade (3 mm and 12 degrees of play, slight drag) until pushed past the point; skewer and pieces never collide. The grill is cold; grill, board and stand are fixed. Cameras render at 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
